reconstructed_theorem_text:
Definition (not a theorem). The displayed object is a real-valued function of a positive natural number n, strictly positive real numbers beta and lambda, and a real number y. Writing this function as F, its value is
F(n, beta, lambda, y) = (n * beta^2 / lambda) * integral from 0 to (lambda * y / (n * beta)) of [g(2 - |s|) / (g(2 - |s|) + g(|s| - 1))] ds,
where g(t) = 0 if t <= 0 and g(t) = exp(-1/t) if t > 0. The natural number n is coerced to a real number in this expression. The integral is the oriented interval integral with respect to real Lebesgue measure, so the definition also includes negative y. No theorem or additional property is asserted.
objects: A real-valued function F of four arguments n, beta, lambda, y; the fixed real-valued auxiliary function g(t), equal to 0 for t <= 0 and exp(-1/t) for t > 0; a real integration variable s.
domains: n is a positive natural number; beta and lambda are strictly positive real numbers, supplied as elements of the positive-real subtype; y and s are real numbers. F takes real values.
quantifiers: There are four function-argument binders, in order n, beta, lambda, y. These are definition binders, not universal quantifiers in a theorem. The integration variable s is locally bound.
assumptions: Only the input-domain restrictions n >= 1, beta > 0, and lambda > 0 are imposed. There is no restriction on y and no additional hypothesis.
conclusion: There is no propositional conclusion. The value assigned to the inputs is exactly (n * beta^2 / lambda) times the oriented integral from 0 to lambda * y / (n * beta) of g(2 - |s|) / (g(2 - |s|) + g(|s| - 1)).
scopes: F is notation introduced here for the entire displayed anonymous function, not a source declaration name. The entire integral is multiplied by n * beta^2 / lambda. The absolute values apply to s. The denominator of the integrand is the sum of both displayed g terms. The auxiliary g has the stated fixed piecewise definition.
constant_dependencies: The numerical constants are fixed: 0 as the lower endpoint and cutoff threshold, 1 and 2 in the cutoff arguments, -1 in exp(-1/t), and exponent 2 on beta. The prefactor depends on n, beta, lambda; the upper endpoint also depends on y. The integrand depends only on s and the fixed g. There is no unspecified constant.
